decision: each hand is compatible with a five-dimensional commuting moment state, but one raw common state across plus and minus requires dimension at least six
mechanism_update: The free shared-rank-five failure is localized to cross-hand pooling.  It is not evidence that either hand separately needs more than five states, and it is not positive evidence for noncommutation.

flat_extension.order1_rank_le_3: fails for both hand blocks and the shared block
flat_extension.order2: unidentified because total-degree-six moments are absent
flat_extension.ordered_path: unidentified because only endpoint displacement is recorded

claim_boundary: The Hankel rank constraints include diagonalizable and Jordan commuting realizations.
The shared-block lower bound applies only when plus and minus are forced to use the same raw transfer state/basis.
Within-hand rank five survives at the frozen threshold; this is compatibility, not proof of exact rank five.
Endpoint Hankel consistency is built into the acquisition and cannot distinguish xy from yx path history.
next_discriminator: extract the covariance-aware degree-two annihilating polynomial/null line separately for plus and minus and test its exact Alexander/C4 transformation, rather than forcing raw shared eigenpairs
